summary: The macro backdrop is mixed-to-hostile for long-duration equities despite strong physical infrastructure demand. Long-end Treasury yields rebounded after the initial buyback relief, energy inflation remains elevated because refining/product disruptions are severe, China is leaning on fiscal infrastructure rather than fresh rate cuts, and copper is physically tight but partly distorted by a flash squeeze.

usRates.read: Restrictive long-end discount rates remain the main valuation headwind for AI/data-centre, grid and robotics growth names. Treasury buybacks improved liquidity but did not solve fiscal/inflation pressure.

energy.read: Crude is geopolitically supported, but the more important current signal is refined-product scarcity. U.S. diesel crack spreads exceeded $100/bbl and global refinery outages keep product inflation elevated.

china.read: Rates were left unchanged for a 15th month. Weak July domestic data persists, but policy is leaning toward accelerated fiscal/infrastructure execution rather than aggressive monetary easing.

metals.read: Copper's structural bottleneck thesis is strengthened, but near-term price action is distorted by concentrated positions, low live LME stocks and U.S.-bound inventory arbitrage. Do not extrapolate squeeze pricing into permanent margins.

riskAssets.read: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell on August 20 as bond yields rebounded, confirming that duration sensitivity remains high even while AI enthusiasm persists.

powerStackImplication: Keep highest conviction in profitable physical bottlenecks with backlog and pricing power. Treat long-duration AI infrastructure and speculative robotics/nuclear developers more tactically while 10Y/30Y yields remain elevated. Refiners retain a stronger near-term setup than generic crude beta. China/HK power and nuclear remain supported by fiscal/state capex, but weak domestic demand argues against a broad cyclical upgrade.
